business_scope.primary_industry_name: Vertical Industrial ERP and Customer Relationship Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with strong Common Law corporate and maritime influences)

Panama-United Kingdom Protocol to the Investment Agreement (effective 2021)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 2015 (Modificada por Ley No. 70 de 2019 y Ley No. 254 de 2021), Decreto Ejecutivo No. 494 de 2015, Decreto Ejecutivo No. 163 de 2020, Acuerdo Medidas Preventivas of the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and Ley No. 25 de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Foundation Incorporation (Certificado de Fundación) - foundatory charter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Público de Panamá / Public Registry of Panama
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama is a contracting party to the Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Foundation's creator (Notaría de Panamá)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing from the Residency Agent
Power of Attorney in favor of the Residency Agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the jurisdiction of the grantor

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notary or issuing authority of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, founders and beneficial settlors against: National sanctions and PEP lists of Panama (UAF), OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Interpol red notices. Compliance with enhanced due diligence obligations imposed by Law 23 of 2015, requiring risk rating, source of funds verification, and independent audit trail retention for minimally 5 years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Sistema de Registro Público en Línea (SIRP) / Oficina de Personas Jurídicas
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be in any language using the Latin alphabet; however the official record requires a Spanish transliteration or pronunciation guide if the name is not in Spanish. Suffixes permitted include 'Fundación', 'Foundation', 'PIF', and must not conflict with existing entries in the Public Registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must file an administrative reconsideration petition (Recurso de Consideración) with the Director General of the Registro Público within 5 working days of formal notification. If the reconsideration is denied, an appealed Recurso de Apelación may be lodged before the Public Registry's Superior Council, and thereafter before the Third Chamber of the Supreme Court of Justice (Corte Suprema de Justicia) as a last resort compliance action.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible for the statutory registered agent and registered office requirements under Articles 19 and 20 of Law 25 of 1995. The registered agent must maintain a physical office in Panama and be licensed. Operational virtual offices for the actual cloud business may be accepted, but they do not constitute corporate commercial substance; substance must be proven via separate contractual arrangements and actual management activities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but possible; estimated annual risk of unannounced physical on-site inspection at the registered office is 5% for this industry, reflecting the standard risk profile for non-regulated low-risk software businesses, subject to UAF discretion in AML/CFT investigations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Law), as amended by Ley No. 49 de 12 de septiembre de 2012; key provisions: Article 1 (foundation powers), Article 4 (constitution methods), Article 7 (minimum endowment), Article 8 (Charter/Rules), Article 12 (Foundation Council), Article 18 (restriction on commercial activity) and Article 24 (Registry inscription)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Fundación de Interés Privado – Escritura Pública Constitutiva y Estatutos (Foundation Charter executed before a Panamanian Notary Public and inscribed in the Foundations Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Foundation must be endowed with a minimum initial capital of USD 10,000.00 (B/.10,000.00) or its equivalent in lawful assets, per Article 7 of Law 25 of 1995. The endowment may be satisfied in cash, movable property, securities or receivables; Panama imposes no mandatory bank escrow for PIFs, but the Notary must certify the actual transfer of the capital into the Foundation's patrimony at execution, and the Public Registry records the declared capital on the inscription certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the initial endowment of USD 10,000.00 contributed by the Founder is accepted and recorded as the Foundation's minimum statutory capital under Law 25 of 1995; (2) that the Foundation's registered office be established at the Registered Agent's offices in Panama City, Republic of Panama; (3) that the persons named in the Foundation Charter are appointed as members of the Foundation Council, with full management powers over the Foundation's assets and authority to enter into software transactions; and (4) that the Council President is authorized to lodge Registry instruments, open bank and escrow accounts, and certify these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Nombre y Reserva Division (online portal www.registropublico.gob.pa or in-person counter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two alternative or numbered designations for the Foundation, each ending in 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or 'Fundación'. The Registry verifies the absence of identical or confusingly similar names in the corporate index and issues a reservation certificate valid for 30 days, extendable once. The Registered Agent executes the search request and collects the official search token.
required_dossiers: Name search and reservation application (Solicitud de Búsqueda y Reserva)
Registered Agent instruction letter
Passport copy of authorizing signatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity, file a new reservation with a distinct denomination or submit a brief written appeal before the Registry's Name Commission within 5 business days; expedited re-filing is available upon payment of the reduced search tariff.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Foundation Charter and Rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública del Primer Circuito de Panamá (First Judicial District Public Notary, Panama City)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Founder and the Registered Agent appear before the Notary and execute the Escritura Pública Constitutiva, together with the Reglamento (Rules/Estatutos). The Instrument must state the Founder's identity, the initial endowment of at least USD 10,000, the Council members, optional Protector, succession and amendment clauses, and the Registered Agent acceptance. The Notary certifies delivery of the endowment and produces certified copies for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Foundation Charter and Rules in Spanish
Name reservation certificate
Passport or ID copies of Founder, Council members and Protector (if any)
Proof or declaration of initial capital contribution
Registered Agent acceptance letter
Background statement of the Founder (customary KYC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary identifies drafting or KYC deficiencies, amend and re-execute the Charter without prejudice; a corrective addendum (Aclaración) may be executed before the same Notary at no additional Registry penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Registry Tariff and Presentation to the Foundations Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado, Central Headquarters
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the official registration fee (B/.250 for the minimum capital bracket) via certified bank draft, and present the certified copies of the notarized Escritura Pública, the Legal Persons Form (Formulario de Persona Jurídica), and the Notary's capital certification. The Registry assigns a folio real number, verifies legal compliance under Law 25, and inscribes the Foundation in the Foundations Section.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarized Escritura Pública Constitutiva
Registry tariff receipt (tarifa registral)
Legal Persons form (Formulario de Persona Jurídica)
Notary certification of the minimum endowment
Founding entity certificate of good standing, caducidad declaration, and compliance declarations if the Founder is a legal person
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a requirement (requerimiento), submit the corrective documentation within 10 business days; if inscription is denied, file a reconsideration appeal (recurso de reconsideración) before the Director General, with a further hierarchical appeal to the Pleno of the Public Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Legal Existence Certificate and Council Authentication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Certifications Window (Ventanilla de Certificaciones)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the inscription is effective, request the Certificado de Fundación (Foundation registration certificate) and, if required, authenticated copies of the inscribed Charter. The certificate evidences juridical personality, the registration number, and registered office. Appointments or resignations of Council members may subsequently be recorded as marginal notes (notas marginales) on the folio.
required_dossiers: Folio real or inscription record number
Written request for certificate (Formulario de Certificación)
Payment of certificate fee (approx. USD 20 plus posting fees)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If discrepancies appear between the certificate and the inscribed Charter, file a rectification application (solicitud de aclaración) with supporting documents; the Registry issues a corrected certificate within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Municipal and Operational Activation of the Vertical Software Business Vehicle
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – RUC Division; Alcaldía del Distrito de Panamá – Rentas Municipales
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because Article 18 of Law 25 restricts direct commercial trading, the Foundation organizes the ISIC 6201 vertical ERP/CRM business through a 100%-owned Panamanian corporation (S.A.). That operating company obtains its RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) with DGI, files the Aviso de Operación with the Municipality, obtains the annual Patente Municipal, and requests the electronic invoicing authorization (Resolución de Facturación Electrónica) before issuing invoices to clients.
required_dossiers: DGI RUC application (Formulario 1-RUC)
Certified copy of the operating company's incorporation certificate
Lease contract or registered office proof
Municipal Aviso de Operación application
Patente Municipal fee schedule and payment receipt
Bank account opening certificate supporting Stripe Billing and Direct Debit rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI or the Municipality returns inconsistency notices, cure by attending the respective tax or municipal regularization desk, pay any applicable transfer tax (ITBMS) registration amount, and re-file within the same fiscal month without late-fee surcharge.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No specialized industrial licensing authority applies to ISIC 6201 (software publishing). The operational registrations are administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance for tax activation, the Alcaldía del Distrito de Panamá – Dirección de Rentas Municipales for the Aviso de Operación and Patente Municipal, and the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) only for commercial registry matters of the operating company.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory industrial license (requires_statutory_license = false). Mandatory operating registrations for the vertical ERP/CRM cloud business: (i) RUC with DGI; (ii) Aviso de Operación and annual Patente Municipal with the Alcaldía; (iii) DGI electronic invoicing authorization (facturación electrónica); and (iv) personal data processing registration before the Autoridad Nacional de Transparencia y Acceso a la Información (ANTAI) under Ley 81 de 2019 if Panamanian customer data is processed.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Category I. Pure software and cloud-hosted SaaS operations are not listed in the mandatory EIA categories of the EIA Regulation (Decreto Ejecutivo No. 123 de 14 de agosto de 2009, as amended); no environmental impact study is required. Administrative registration with MiAMBIENTE becomes necessary only if the operator installs a local server room with auxiliary fuel storage or rooftop telecommunications equipment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or industrial discharge is generated by vertical ERP/CRM cloud operations. If an office or server room is maintained: compliance with Ley No. 138 de 2018 (integrated waste management) for e-waste and used batteries; domestic wastewater discharge limits under MiAMBIENTE water quality resolutions applicable to municipal sewer connections; any emergency generator diesel tank must meet secondary containment standards and the Cuerpo de Bomberos inspection threshold; UPS battery disposal must be contracted to an authorized hazardous waste recycler.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de la República de Panamá: mandatory fire safety inspection and Fire Code compliance certificate (Permiso de Seguridad Contra Incendios) for the registered office and any server room. Municipal permitting authority: structural load inspection and construction permit validation if rooftop antenna, cooling or UPS equipment is installed. Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL): occupational health and safety workplace registration and, for payroll of 25 or more employees, mandatory internal safety and hygiene committee. Caja de Seguro Social (CSS): employer registration and payroll affiliation for all Panamanian staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); electronic portal: e-Tax (https://e-tax.gob.pa). Customs-side authority: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas de Panamá (ANA) via SICE (Sistema Integrado de Comercio Exterior).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The foreign-owned PIF must obtain a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente). Procedure: (1) execute the Pacto Fundacional with a licensed Panama resident agent and register the foundation at the Public Registry; (2) file the DGI RUC application (assigning the economic activity to ISIC 6201) attaching the certified foundation deed, registered agent acceptance, and municipal Aviso de Operación where commercial activity is intended; (3) obtain a Firma Electrónica Avanzada digital certificate; (4) activate, through e-Tax, the ISR (income tax) and ITBMS registers and appoint a local tax representative where the foundation board is non-resident. Processing period: approximately 5 to 10 business days; RUC issuance typically completes within 1 to 3 business days after document validation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope — Entity-level taxation confined to Panama-source income. Foreign-source dividends, interest, capital gains, and offshore software services of the PIF are outside the Panamanian tax base; Panama-source activity (local ERP/CRM sales to Panamanian customers) triggers ISR at 25% on net taxable profit and ITBMS at 7%. A foundation confined to estate-planning assets with no Panama-source activity holds a de facto non-taxable status rather than a statutory tax-exempt certificate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not administer a U.S.-style check-the-box election, nor an elective hybrid-mismatch regime. Available statutory elections: (i) election, within the foundation instrument, to operate as a purely private estate-planning vehicle vs. a commercial entity (commercial status requires the municipal Aviso de Operación and full DGI registration); (ii) election to be assessed under the simplified ITBMS quota regime where annual gross taxable receipts are B/. 200,000 or less; (iii) election to accede to the DGI large-taxpayer compliance group (Grandes Contribuyentes); and (iv) election of the taxable year and tax-consolidation parameters only as prescribed by the Código Fiscal. No free classification choice exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT-type transfer tax — ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencias de Bienes Muebles y Servicios), Law 43 of 2005 as amended, including Law 187 of 2019 on digital services and the digital-platform registration rules for non-residents.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 0 — no de minimis turnover exemption; any person carrying out taxable transfers of goods or rendering taxable services in Panama must register for ITBMS before the DGI and file monthly returns. A reduced simplified regime (fixed quota) is accessible where annual gross receipts do not exceed B/. 200,000 (approximately USD 200,000); non-resident digital service providers must also register via e-Tax and appoint a responsible local agent for Panama-source digital services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing through the DGI 'Facturación Electrónica de Panamá' system under a phased mandate covering all registered taxpayers. Taxpayers must obtain DGI authorization for each fiscal invoice series, transmit invoice XML transactions to the DGI validation web-service/API, and incorporate a digital certificate signature plus QR/código de seguridad on each document. The model is authorization-and-validation (near-real-time), not continuous cryptographic stamping; smaller taxpayers may use the DGI free e-Tax invoicing module while large taxpayers must use certified fiscal operators.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: ITBMS zero-rating is available to: (1) exporters of tangible goods whose physical departure from Panama is evidenced in SICE; and (2) providers of services used exclusively abroad, including offshore cloud ERP/CRM subscriptions where the contracting counterparty, place of effective use, and invoicing address are non-Panamanian. Digital services supplied for use in Panama are outside zero-rating and attract 7% ITBMS, including supplies by non-residents under Law 187 of 2019. To assert 0%, the PIF must evidence the foreign economic destination through the service contract, service-scope documentation, and customer non-residence certificates.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Panama Customs Export Declaration filed in SICE (Declaración de Exportación)
Bill of Lading / Sea Waybill or Air Waybill as transport evidence
Commercial Invoice and Packing List (for goods; services are instead substantiated by the foreign service contract and usage report)
Inward Remittance / bank transfer certificate evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Foreign non-residence certificate or equivalent tax-ID proof of the offshore ERP/CRM customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI examines zero-rating and ITBMS credit claims through post-clearance audits that cross-match SICE export declarations, service contracts, bank credits, and monthly ITBMS returns. Missing or contradicted documentation, fictitious exports, or failure to substantiate effective offshore use within the administrative review trigger: (i) immediate reinstatement of 7% ITBMS plus moratory interest; (ii) administrative fines under the Código Fiscal from B/. 1,000 to B/. 100,000 and surcharges of up to 100% of the evaded tax for concealment; (iii) late-filing and under-declaration penalties assessed via e-Tax; and (iv) criminal tax-fraud proceedings where intent or forged documents are proven. The reassessment limitation period is generally 5 years, extended where fraudulent concealment or non-registration is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) as the banking and financial supervision authority; Banco Nacional de Panamá as the State's fiscal agent. Panama maintains no issuing central bank or exchange-control regulator; monetary operations are conducted under the dollarized legal-tender framework in which the US Dollar circulates as lawful currency alongside the Balboa monetary unit pegged 1:1.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized monetary system. The US Dollar is legal tender and the Balboa exists solely as a nominal unit for copper coins. Capital and current account transactions are fully convertible and unrestricted: there are no exchange controls, no prior approval requirements, and no withholding or restrictions on profit repatriation, capital distributions, loan servicing, or portfolio transfers. Foreign-currency accounts—including USD, EUR, GBP, and CNY—are freely permitted at SBP-supervised banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Panama imposes no statutory surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts or any other FX proceeds. Software export revenue and cloud subscription receipts may be retained in any currency, in any jurisdiction, and repatriated to a Panamanian bank account at any time without central-bank authorization.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium with material constraints. Panama's SBP-supervised fintech regime (including the financial innovation hub and sandbox licensing for clearing services) does not permit a purely offshore EMI to access SIPE local clearing or ACH rails without holding a banking, payment, or crypto-related license under SBP rules. Offshore EMIs such as Wise or Payoneer may be used as pass-through collection wallets for non-Panamanian SaaS revenue, but inbound credits from these EMIs into Tier-1 Panamanian accounts trigger enhanced AML review, third-party-funding flags, and frequent compliance holds. Viable strategy: use a licensed Panamanian payment service provider or a merchant-of-record arrangement (Stripe Billing) with direct settlement to a Banco General or Banistmo operational account, avoiding EMI routing as the primary treasury rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical board appearance is not statutorily mandatory. SBP AML rules (Ley 23/2015, Decree Law 2/2011 and Agreement No. 004-2017) require documented client identification, source-of-funds evidence, and a face-to-face or equivalent video-interview completed by the compliance officer. In practice Tier-1 banks accept remote onboarding for a Panama Private Interest Foundation when the application is introduced by a licensed Registered Agent (law firm) and at least one Foundation Council member completes a notarized power of attorney and a video KYC call. Some banks nevertheless require an in-person visit to the branch for the first account activation or for the opening of Capital Escrow accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foundation provides structured privacy: public registry shows only the Registered Agent and name; Beneficial Owner is not on the public foundational deed.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide notarized Foundation Charter (Acta Fundacional) and Reglamento; certified Registry Certificate of Private Interest Foundation (Certificado de Personería Jurídica); sealed Beneficial-owner declaration maintained by the Registered Agent under Ley 23/2015; legal opinion from Panamanian counsel on the foundation's legal personality and the justified use of a private foundation; and MPC semi-annual capital movement declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border SaaS subscription receipts flowing from multiple jurisdictions through Stripe Billing with no single dominant client and short sales history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed vertical-ERP/CRM enterprise agreements with ISIC 6201 scope; auditable revenue projection model; monthly Stripe settlement statements reconciled to SWIFT MT103 credits; PCI-DSS compliance certificate; SBP account application containing the full business narrative; and an express undertaking by the AML officer to allow transaction-pattern monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection from founder with foreign jurisdiction wealth and no Panamanian tax record, triggering source-of-funds queries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statement and reference letter from the founder's source bank; certified net-worth statement or CPA-prepared opening balance sheet; founder's tax filings in jurisdiction of residence; notarized source-of-funds declaration; matching SWIFT MT103 advice showing the exact inbound capital wire; and proof of payment of applicable stamp taxes in Panama.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency and CRS/FATCA ambiguity: the PIF is treated as a hybrid entity by the foreign parent group while claiming territorial tax non-liability in Panama.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Panama Tax Residency Certificate from DGI (Dirección General de Ingresos) if substance exists; Fiscal Code territorial-tax analysis by counsel; CRS/FATCA self-certification forms for the foundation and all substantial owners; report of economic substance (local office lease, payroll, IT equipment, server-level operations for the Vertical Cloud) or, if offshore-administered, a robust non-residency position backed by a registered representative.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound founder capital or shareholder advances are delivered by SWIFT MT103 using the beneficiary account at the Panamanian bank. Panama requires no central-bank approval and imposes no admission tax or waiting period for capital contributions. The remittance narrative should state 'Capital contribution to Private Interest Foundation — Ley 25 de 1995' and the SBP statistical transaction type for inward direct investment (Code 61/62) or, for working-capital advances, Code 58 'Business services — ISIC 6201'. The bank will require the Foundation Charter, Registry Certificate, Beneficial-owner declaration, source-of-funds evidence, and validation that the remitter is a named founder or a shareholder of the foundation. Crediting occurs same-day through SIPE US-dollar clearing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and treasury settlements are executed via SWIFT MT103 and MT202 COV for infrastructure procurement, licensor fees, subcontracting and software acquisition; Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit (UCP 600) are available through Panamanian banks and the Panama Chamber of Commerce for larger capital goods. Domestic USD payments settle via SIPE and ACH Panamá for payroll and tax remittances to DGI and CSS (social security). For recurring inbound collections, the recommended rails are Stripe Billing with a Panamanian merchant of record or direct-debit initiation through a licensed payment processor into the foundation's bank account. The service exports qualify for territorial tax treatment and no Panama withholding is applied to software royalty outflows under ISIC 6201.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable USD/EUR, USD/GBP and USD/CNY FX forwards offered by SBP-licensed Panamanian banks (e.g., Banco General, Multibank) to lock cloud-infrastructure procurement costs — no central-bank approval required.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) against Latin American non-deliverable currencies (COP, MXN, BRL) for regional subscription inflows, executed with SBP-supervised or international bank branches under ISDA 2002 terms.

Cross-currency swaps (XCCY) matching USD operating liabilities against EUR/GBP subscription revenue streams where grouped entities invoice in those currencies, subject to ISDA/CSA collateral arrangements.

FX vanilla options and futures executed only with regulated counterparties; derivatives entered for genuine hedging of non-USD software licensing receipts are unrestricted for non-financial corporations, while speculative positions may be limited by bank treasury credit policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Tasa Unica Anual B/.300) for the Panama Private Interest Foundation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economia y Finanzas; payment recorded by the Public Registry of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between January 2 and June 30 covering the current calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a 10% surcharge plus statutory default interest; three consecutive unpaid years expose the foundation to administrative strike-off or dissolution by the Public Registry, which also withholds certificates of good standing pending full settlement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of updated beneficial ownership and foundation council records to the resident agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Resident Agent (licensed Panamanian attorney or firm); Unidad de Analisis Financiero (UAF) may request production under Law 23 of 2015
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually at registration anniversary and within 30 calendar days of any change in beneficiaries, foundation council members, or registered assets
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under Law 23 of 2015 and associated AML regulations, up to USD 50,000 for serious non-compliance; non-maintained UBO records place the foundation and its resident agent outside AML good standing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renewal of resident agent and registered office services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Private contractual renewal with the Panamanian resident agent; no separate filing with the Public Registry is required for the renewal itself
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the foundation's registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss or lapse of the resident agent is a statutory ground for administrative strike-off; all registry notices become unreachable and the foundation may be dissolved ex officio

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit applies to a passive asset-holding PIF without Panama-source income; a certified independent audit becomes mandatory only when the foundation carries on taxable commercial activity in Panama with gross Panama-source revenue equal to or greater than B/.1,500,000, when required by the foundation charter, or when demanded by a Panamanian court, licensing authority, or financing institution
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), including IFRS for SMEs as adopted in Panama; Panama's Codigo de Comercio (Article 72) requires statutory accounting books to be preserved for 10 years, while the 7-year retention window adopted by this matrix exceeds the 5-year DGI tax prescription period and is administratively acceptable

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 23 of 2015 and the 2022 Supreme Court ruling declaring the centralized UBO registry unconstitutional, beneficial ownership documentation for the PIF is maintained exclusively at the resident agent's office and disclosed only upon lawful request of the UAF, DGI, or judicial authority. The agent must obtain certified identification for all beneficiaries and foundation council members at formation and refresh it at each annual renewal; any interest transfer or change in beneficiary entitlement must be evidenced by a formal foundation council resolution and communicated to the resident agent within 30 calendar days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (for PIF: Register of Beneficiaries)
Register of Directors (for PIF: Register of Foundation Council)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas of Foundation Council Resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600-1,500 per annum typical market range for Panama resident agent and registered office
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable for a non-commercial holding PIF; voluntary or bank-requested certified audit typically USD 3,000-8,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial tax regime: income sourced or activity occurring in Panama is taxable at 25%; bona fide foreign-source income is outside the tax base, producing a 0% effective tax on non-Panama receipts. Statutory incentives include tax holidays and preferential regimes for companies licensed under Panama-Pacifico, Ciudad del Saber, and Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regimes. A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) maintained for lawful estate/asset holding is tax-neutral on distributions derived from foreign-source assets; no Panamanian income tax is levied on the PIF's principal or on distributions to beneficiaries unless the PIF realizes Panamanian-source income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 101 (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta para Personas Jurídicas) filed electronically through the DGI T@S tax portal; mandatory for Panamanian legal entities, including Private Interest Foundations that have Panamanian-source income or that choose to file to preserve tax status.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly advance income tax returns (Formulario 104 / ITBT) are required for taxpayers whose gross Panamanian-source revenue exceeds US$1.5 million.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the annual return is due by 31 March of the following year; for any other fiscal year-end, the return is due within three months after the close of the taxable year. The DGI generally does not grant blanket extensions for corporate income tax returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC number and taxpayer identification, registered name, fiscal agent / legal representative details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIF must obtain a RUC and disclose the registered agent and legal representative. If the PIF has no Panamanian-source activity, it may be registered as a non-commercial holder but must still file the annual sworn return where Panamanian filing obligations apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable year and fiscal period, in accordance with the governing instruments and accounting books.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the fiscal year set out in the PIF charter. For non-resident-controlled PIFs, a 31 December year-end is standard; any other date requires consistency in books and prior DGI-conformity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panama-source gross revenue: subscriptions, licenses, software-as-a-service fees, service commissions, IP royalties, and other income whose use or economic realization occurs in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Panamanian-source receipts. Pure foreign-source revenue earned from offshore clients outside Panama is excludable based on the territoriality principle; documentary evidence of situs must be maintained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: direct costs, expenses, depreciation, amortization, and allocable overhead strictly necessary to produce Panamanian-source income; expenses must meet the general deduction requirements and be supported by invoices and documents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PIF may deduct expenses only to the extent attributable to Panamanian-source income. Expenses related to foreign assets or foreign portfolio management are not deductible in the Panamanian return because the corresponding income is outside scope.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after application of allowable deductions and up to five years of net operating loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the PIF's sole activity is conservative asset holding with no Panamanian-source income, report zero taxable income and attach a short narrative and evidence that no activity generated Panamanian-source revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax calculation: net taxable income multiplied by 25% corporate rate, reduced by advance tax payments, foreign tax credits, and Panamanian-source withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PIF should claim credit only for Panamanian-source withholdings already collected. Foreign taxes cannot be credited against Panamanian tax on foreign-source income because that income is outside Panama's territorial tax net.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividend withholding tax reconciliation if the PIF or its commercial subsidiary distributed Panamanian-source profits to shareholders or beneficiaries during the period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PIF distributions representing return of foundation capital or distributions of foreign-source assets are not dividend payments for Panamanian tax purposes. Panamanian-source profits distributed through a Panamanian company trigger the 10% dividend withholding tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or failure to file the Formulario 101 triggers a fine of 10% of the tax payable, plus monthly interest charges and surcharges on unpaid tax, and additional administrative sanctions. Willful omission of Panamanian-source income can elevate the case to tax fraud with penalties of 5–8 years imprisonment and fines of up to three times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Double Taxation Agreement (DTA) reduction or exemption, the beneficial owner must: (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC, Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) from the treaty country tax authority; (ii) complete and submit the standard DGI beneficial ownership declaration / Form 890-BG or equivalent form required at the time of filing; (iii) notify the Panamanian payer and customs of tax office before payment; and (iv) retain the TRC, the DGI receipt, and the beneficial ownership statement for at least five years. Reduced treaty rates apply at source only when the payer has the required originals or certified copies; if the full 10% is withheld, the non-resident must file an annual refund claim with the DGI within the statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic withholding tax rate is 12.5% when paid to a non-resident for Panamanian-source IP use (software licensing, trademarks, patents, know-how). Interest: contractual interest paid to non-residents from Panamanian-source loans is subject to 12.5% withholding, with certain exemptions for registered bank deposits and institutional financing; treaty rates generally reduce the applicable rate to 5%–10% for interest and 5%–12.5% for royalties depending on the DTA.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: US$3,000,000 (B/.3,000,000) gross annual revenue for mandatory Local File and Master File documentation; country-by-country reporting threshold is consolidated group revenue equal to or greater than US$850,000,000. Panamanian taxpayers executing cross-border related-party transactions above the threshold must file the annual transfer pricing informative return and all OECD-compliant documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (Law 254 of 2019 and its implementing amendments) apply to tax-resident Panamanian legal entities, including Private Interest Foundations, that carry on a relevant activity (IP exploitation, holding assets, distribution and services, financing and leasing, or headquarters activity). The doctrine requires real physical presence in Panama, qualified local employees, sufficient premises, local management meetings, and substantiated local expenditure proportionate to the income. A PIF whose only activity is passive holding of foreign IP without a Panamanian commercial substance is treated as a shell and exposed to annual ESR reporting, economic substance review, deregistration, and administrative fines. A PIF that generates no Panamanian-source income and is not tax-resident is generally outside the ESR scope, but the DGI may reclassify it if management decisions are effectively taken in Panama.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful omission of Panamanian-source revenue, false deduction claims, creation of fictitious invoices, concealment of cloud subscription receipts received in Panama, or filing a knowingly false Formulario 101.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud penalty: imprisonment for 5 to 8 years, restitution of evaded tax, and a fine equal to three times the tax evaded; civil tax liability includes the unpaid principal plus interest and 10% late-filing penalties. The court may also impose temporary closure of the taxpayer's Panamanian operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, foundation council members, and registered agents who sign or cause false returns to be filed are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and fines if the corporate veil is pierced for fraud. Criminal judges may impose asset embargos, travel bans, and prevent foreign transfer of PIF assets pending trial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Economic Substance Avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Panamanian Private Interest Foundation as a phantom owner of IP or as a conduit for CRM/ERP licensing income while all formation, management, and board decisions take place outside Panama and no local office or staff is maintained, causing EU/DR CNS obligations to be circumvented.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the ESR and anti-shell rules, the DGI can require annual ESR filings, impose non-compliance fines of up to USD 100,000 per filing violation, strike the entity from the public registry, and reclassify past foreign-source income as Panamanian taxable income on the basis of effective management in Panama. Repeat offenders face license revocation and professional disqualification of the resident agent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Any director or administrator who knowingly uses the PIF as a sham to conceal beneficial ownership is jointly liable for the reassessed tax and ESR fines. Courts may issue travel bans and passport restrictions against directors, and the Public Registry may be judicially directed to cancel the foundation registration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PIF to approve payments to undisclosed beneficiaries, issuing bearer contracts or opaque corporate structures with no beneficial ownership declaration, processing software license fees from unknown sources, or failing to maintain KYC and transaction records as required by Law 23/2015 and the AML regulations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering predicate offense under Panama's Penal Code and Law 23/2015 can be punished by imprisonment from 8 to 22 years for aggravated cases, plus confiscation of assets and fines of up to USD 1,000,000 for institutional failures; the registered agent can also lose its professional license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who conceal beneficial owners or who execute suspicious cross-border transfers are exposed to criminal indictment, personal financial liability through asset recovery orders, travel bans, preventive detention, and disqualification from serving on Panamanian foundations or companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting non-arm's-length royalties, interest, or service fees between the PIF and related Panamanian operating companies; absence of contemporaneous Local/Master File documentation; arbitrary allocation of ERP/CRM licensing costs; or invoicing for services that are not actually rendered in Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may adjust taxable income to arm's length, disallow base-eroding payments, impose a 30% surcharge on the additional tax determined, plus monthly interest, and levy administrative penalties for failure to file transfer pricing documentation. Significant and deliberate manipulation may be charged as criminal tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing certificates or who approve fictitious intercompany royalty structures are jointly liable for the adjustment and fines. In serious cases, bankruptcy of the Panamanian entity triggers civil liability for breach of fiduciary duty and criminal sanction for fraudulent insolvency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful Profit Distribution and Director Mismanagement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Authorizing distributions from Panamanian-source profits without reserving and paying the 10% dividend withholding tax, or causing the PIF to distribute capital in excess of the foundation's assets to the prejudice of creditors or beneficiaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unpaid dividend tax attracts a penalty equal to 10% of the omitted tax plus monthly interest, and the DGI may uncannily reclassify distributions as taxable dividends and assess the 10% tax on the gross amount. Violation of foundation rules may also expose directors to civil liability for unauthorized distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorize non-compliant distributions are personally liable to the PIF and its creditors for the amount unlawfully distributed. The court may pierce the foundation's veil, impose an asset embargo, prohibit leaving Panama, and convert the civil case into a criminal indictment for breach of trust or fraudulent administration.
